encounters.cc: Fever, productive cough, and dyspnea requiring hospitalization for community-acquired pneumonia

lines: Fever, productive cough, and dyspnea requiring hospitalization for community-acquired pneumonia
He has been febrile and mildly tachypneic for two days but is hemodynamically stable and receiving ceftriaxone and azithromycin.
During hospitalization, his glucose levels are monitored every 6 hours, and he is transitioned from his outpatient oral medications to a subcutaneous insulin regimen.
On hospital day 3, he receives his scheduled dose of insulin glargine in the morning.
A few hours later, a nurse notes that his serum glucose has dropped from 228 mg/dL to 112 mg/dL without any change in IV fluids or food intake.
The patient remains alert and asymptomatic.
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 4 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
- Acetaminophen 650 mg orally every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease
Alcohol: Social drinker (1-2 drinks per week).
Physical exam is unremarkable, and there is no evidence of lipodystrophy or insulin overdosage.
The team suspects this reflects a pharmacologic effect of the insulin dose.

encounters.cc: Fatigue, poor exercise tolerance, dizziness, and metallic taste

lines: Fatigue, poor exercise tolerance, dizziness, and metallic taste

The patient is a 66-year-old male with long-standing diabetic nephropathy and history of tertiary hyperparathyroidism who presents with fatigue, poor exercise tolerance, and occasional dizziness over the past few months.
He also notes loss of appetite and a metallic taste, and stopped NSAIDs recently due to worsening kidney function.
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 4 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
He has a history of diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and osteoarthritis.
Medications include insulin, lisinopril, and acetaminophen.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease
Exam shows pale conjunctivae and decreased vibratory sensation in the feet.
Labs reveal hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, MCV 89 fL, reticulocyte count 0.4%, creatinine 5.1 mg/dL, and GFR 14 mL/min/1.73 m².
Ferritin, transferrin saturation, TSH, B12, and folate are normal.
Peripheral smear shows normocytic RBCs without abnormalities.

lines: Non-healing ulcer on plantar surface of right foot for 3 months
The patient with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Stage 4 CKD, and prior tertiary hyperparathyroidism returns for podiatry evaluation.
He reports that the ulcer has been present for 3 months and has gradually increased in size.
He denies any fever or chills but mentions a dull ache in the area.
His diabetes has been poorly controlled with a recent HbA1c of 9.2%.
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 4 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
- Acetaminophen 650 mg orally every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease
Alcohol: Social drinker (1-2 drinks per week).
On physical examination, the ulcer measures 3 cm in diameter, with a calloused edge and minimal surrounding erythema.
Sensation is decreased in a stocking-glove distribution, and dorsalis pedis pulses are diminished bilaterally.

encounters.cc: Increasing shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea

lines: Increasing shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea

The patient is a 72-year-old man with a known history of coronary artery disease status post inferior wall STEMI in 2025, chronic kidney disease stage 4 with prior tertiary hyperparathyroidism and anemia of chronic disease, and long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus complicated by prior osteomyelitis of the foot, who is brought to the emergency department by his daughter due to increasing shortness of breath over the past week.
He reports difficulty breathing when lying flat and now sleeps upright in a recliner.
He also notes waking up at night gasping for air and a recent reduction in his ability to walk short distances without becoming winded.
He denies fever, cough, or chest pain.
He has not had any recent medication changes and does not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs.
His daughter notes that he has appeared increasingly fatigued and has had swelling in his feet and ankles that worsens throughout the day.
He has also complained of needing to urinate more frequently at night.
His appetite is reduced, but he has not experienced weight loss, nausea, or vomiting.
- Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) of inferior wall (diagnosed 2025-01-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 4 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His past medical history includes coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and long-standing hypertension.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Sevelamer carbonate 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
- Acetaminophen 650 mg orally every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease
He has not had any recent medication changes and does not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs.
His heart rate is 104/min and regular. Blood pressure is 138/82 mm Hg.
On physical examination, he appears dyspneic and uses accessory muscles to breathe.
Auscultation reveals end-expiratory crackles at the bases of both lungs.
There is no wheezing or rhonchi.
His heart rate is 104/min and regular, with a displaced apical impulse and soft S1.
A third heart sound (S3) is audible at the apex.
Jugular venous distension is observed with the head of the bed elevated to 45 degrees.
There is bilateral 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities extending to the mid-shin.
The abdomen is soft and non-tender, and there is no hepatosplenomegaly.
Chest x-ray shows bilateral perihilar opacities with a "bat-wing" distribution and Kerley B lines.
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy.
